text: In this game, you will be using metaphors as clues for the other player to guess who you are describing.

How to play:

  1. Player 1 thinks of a person both players know. You must really know them (you can’t use a famous person) because it really helps if you know them really well.
  2. Player 2 asks questions to help them find out which person Player 1 is thinking of. But all the questions must use metaphors. Here are some examples:
    • What colour are they?
    • What animal are they?
    • What taste are they?
    • What film are they?
    • What biscuit are they?
    • What chair are they?
  3. Player 1 answers the question, thinking carefully about what the person is really like. Player 1 must say a one-word answer. Here’s an example:
    • Player 1 thinks: Grandma.
    • Player 2 says: What chair are they?
    • Player 1 thinks: If Grandma was a chair, she’d be a sofa because she’s comforting, and it feels safe and cosy being with her.
    • Player 1 says: Sofa
  4. Player 2 keeps asking questions until they feel sure they know who it is. It’s best to ask a few more questions after you think you know so that you can be really certain!
  5. When Player 2 has guessed correctly, swap over and have another game!
